_notes: Shipped defaults for pfSense-pkg-gamedetect. The live file is /usr/local/etc/gamedetect/signatures.json; edit that one, not this.
Format and authoring guide: docs/signatures.md in the package source.
Keys starting with _ are ignored by the loader.

Weights: dns 50-60, port_and_prefix 30-40, prefix 10-20, plain port 20-25. A plain port rule (not scoped to a prefix set) stays below low (30) so a broad range alone never labels a title (UDP 5060 SIP is not League, 3074 is not always Call of Duty); only a title-unique port may reach low alone (minecraft_bedrock 19132-19133, 35). dns+port reaches medium (dns 50) or high (dns 60); port+prefix reaches low.

Prefix sets are BGP-announced IPv4 prefixes of the publisher's own ASN (Valve publishes its list). Publishers that host on public clouds (Epic, EA, Activision, Mojang, NetEase overseas) have no prefix set on purpose: whole-cloud ranges would match everything.
No title claims UDP 443, so QUIC stays filtered.

Known limitation: marvel_rivals is NOT detectable from flow rules alone. Its port 9000-9999 rule is a weight-10 placeholder (below low), so it only shows when its DNS matches (60+10=70, medium); clients that bypass the resolver stay unknown.
Unverified DNS globs (guesses at what the client resolves in play, not captured): overwatch2, wow, cs2 (*.counter-strike.net), dota2 (*.dota2.com), apex, battlefield, marvel_rivals (*.easebar.com).
Roblox 49152-65535 is the OS ephemeral range, so it is a port_and_prefix rule on the roblox set: a plain port rule would let any WebRTC/P2P flow unlock the Roblox DNS points.
Riot voice (UDP 27016-27024, 54000-54012) is a port_and_prefix rule of the generic riot title on the riot set so it outscores the Valve 27000-27250 port rule on Riot IPs.

Publisher-generic titles (steam, riot) own the evidence every title of a publisher shares: its network, its port ranges and (riot) its launcher/anti-cheat DNS. The specific titles keep the same flow rules at weight 5 each (flow-only 10, never labelled) and are named by a game-specific dns rule (60). riot: Riot client and Vanguard names (*.riotgames.com, *.riotcdn.net, *.pvp.net, *.rgpub.io*) are resolved for LoL and Valorant alike, and LoL's game servers use 7000-8000 like Valorant (live: 192.207.0.5:7193), so port + prefix + generic dns = 60 is 'Riot game' (medium); lol/valorant also carry the generic dns rule (20) and win with their specific name: 60 + 20 + 10 = 90 vs 60. LoL's specific names: *.leagueoflegends.com and lolstatic*.akamaihd.net* (the cache shows the CNAME-flattened lolstatic-a.akamaihd.net.edgesuite.net). LoL vs Valorant is only told apart while the client holds a connection to a game-specific host.

Valve network traffic (UDP 27000-27250 and/or the valve prefix set) is shared by every Steam title that uses Steam Datagram Relay, so it scores the generic title steam (port 25 + prefix 15 = 40, low). cs2 and dota2 carry the same flow rules at weight 5 each (flow-only 10, never labelled) and are named only by their DNS rule (60; with the flow rules 70, which also stays > 10 ahead of source_engine's 55 when the client binds 27005): a TF2 or Deadlock player on the Valve network is 'Steam / Valve game', not 'Valve (Counter-Strike 2 or Dota 2)'.

dns_optional: a title with "dns_optional": true has no dns rule on purpose. steam: every PC with Steam open resolves the Steam domains, so they say nothing about what is being played. source_engine: community servers (TF2, GMod, CS:S, L4D2) are bare IPs on rented hosts with no DNS name.

source_engine keys on the Source client port: Source games bind UDP 27005 locally (clientport) and pf keeps it pre-NAT, so src_port 27005 alone is 40 (low) on any host; with a Source server or Valve relay port 27015-27150 (Source servers default to 27015+, Valve's SDR relay config uses 27015-27140) it is 55 (medium). It cannot tell TF2, GMod, CS:S or L4D2 apart. On a Valve relay (27015-27150) it scores 55 against steam 40, so the client port wins; on a relay port above 27150 both are 40 and the client is unknown.

False positives: an idle Steam client that keeps a UDP flow to the Valve network can read as 'Steam / Valve game' (low). A random local port that happens to be 27005 (e.g. after a second NAT in front of the client) gives a false 'Source engine game' (low).

Low-confidence entries (port data is secondhand or missing, tune from the Unclassified tab): fortnite port 9000-9100, lol/riot port 5000-5500 (Riot's old docs; live LoL used 7193), cod dst ports, battlefield ports, marvel_rivals port, wow (gameplay is TCP 1119/3724; UDP is voice only).
